title: Video Games: From Jumpman to Blocks
description: A green brother, a carpenter who became a plumber, a company older than airplanes, and the best-selling game ever—five pixel steps.

questions.question: He wears green, and his name sounds like the Japanese word for "similar." Who is Mario's brother?
questions.explanation: Luigi started in 1983's Mario Bros. as a green copy of Mario so two friends could play together. "Ruiji" means similar in Japanese—a lucky naming accident!

questions.question: Luigi's brother Mario first appeared—as a carpenter named Jumpman—in what arcade game?
questions.explanation: Back in 1981 he was Jumpman the carpenter, not a plumber! Nintendo later named him after Mario Segale, the landlord of its warehouse in America.

questions.question: Donkey Kong was made by which Japanese company—that started in 1889 making flower playing cards?
questions.explanation: Nintendo started in Kyoto making hanafuda cards—before airplanes were even invented. Video games came almost a century later. The company is older than the zipper!

questions.question: Nintendo's handheld with two screens had what two-letter name—short for Dual Screen?
questions.explanation: Nintendo sold about 154 million DS systems. It was Nintendo's best-selling console ever—until the Switch finally passed it in 2025.

questions.question: The Switch beat the DS, but the best-selling video game of all time isn't made by Nintendo at all! What blocky building game is it?
questions.hint: You mine blocks and craft tools
questions.explanation: Minecraft has sold more than 350 million copies—more than any other video game ever. It started in 2009 at a small studio in Sweden called Mojang.
